transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Hartley Museum, Education Department. Sarah Fraser speaking.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Hello, my name is Paul Reed. I teach history at Greenfield School, and I'd like to bring a class of Year 9 students to the museum next month.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Lovely. How many students are there?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Twenty-eight, plus three adults. We were thinking of Tuesday the eleventh, but that depends on what's available.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Let me check. Tuesday the eleventh is fully booked, I'm afraid. We do have Wednesday the twelfth or Friday the fourteenth.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Friday's better for us because it's the last lesson before the weekend and students won't miss a test. Can we have the morning?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes, ten o'clock. The visit lasts about two hours, including a workshop. What's your topic?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: We're studying the Roman occupation of Britain, so the Roman gallery is the main thing.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Perfect. We have a workshop called Life in a Roman Fort, where students handle real objects and try on replica armour. It costs three pounds fifty per student, and the adults come free.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That's reasonable. Is the workshop in addition to the entrance fee?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: School groups don't pay an entrance fee. So the total would be ninety-eight pounds.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Good. Do you offer a worksheet or something to keep the students focused?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: We do. Our teacher pack has a worksheet and a quiz. I can email it to you in advance so you can prepare.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That would be very helpful. And how do we get there? The school has no minibus.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: The number twenty-one bus stops outside the museum. Many schools use it. Alternatively, there's a coach parking bay on Kent Street.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: We'll use a coach. Is there anything I need to do about accessibility? One of my students uses a wheelchair.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: The whole museum is accessible, and there's a lift to every floor. However, the Roman gallery has a very narrow door, so I'd suggest she goes through the side entrance. A member of staff will help.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Thank you. What should I do to confirm the booking?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I'll send a form today. Return it within seven days with a deposit of twenty pounds, and your place is secure. If you need to cancel, please let us know at least a week before the visit so another school can take your slot.
